card.summary: No account: the search feed at /?page=rss&q=... returned RSS 2.0 with a nyaa namespace and per-item torrent links.

record.category: torrent index, anime and East Asian media (RSS, no account)

free_tier.stated: No account: the search feed at /?page=rss&q=... returned RSS 2.0 with a nyaa namespace and per-item torrent links.

per_object_cap.stated: the tracker caps a single torrent file and the site caps uploads, neither of which is a client-side limit on the index
per_object_cap.notes: the caps were not read on the pages fetched

retention.stated: releases persist; the feed returns only the query's matches, so age is not implied by the feed

egress.terms: no byte allowance: the feed serves XML and .torrent links; the transfer is client-to-swarm

record.interface_detail: RSS at /?page=rss with the usual query parameters (q, c, f); each item's <link> is a .torrent download and <guid> is the view page.
record.tooling: Any RSS reader; the item link is already the .torrent, so no page fetch is needed.
record.chaining: A saved search as an RSS feed is the cheapest possible subscription: one URL per interest is polled and returns .torrent links, which a debrid service then turns into cached playback.

limits.value: none published on the pages fetched; the feed answered immediately with no 429

record.limits_note: The feed is the whole interface: no key, no token, no pagination wall on the routes tried.
record.binding_note: No byte accounting exists on an index; polling a saved search is a handful of requests a day, far below anything that would throttle.

identity_cost.detail: No account for search or RSS; uploading and commenting need one, which is not needed here.

record.reliability_note: A query with no match returns a valid feed with zero items rather than an error, so a client must check item count rather than status. The one match for 'ubuntu' was dated 2009, so the index holds very old items and a fresh-looking feed says nothing about freshness.
record.confidence_note: The feed was fetched on 2026-10-23 and parsed: one item for 'ubuntu', with a .torrent link. A month of polling would raise it to measured.

evidence.proved: RSS 2.0 with the nyaa namespace, channel title 'Nyaa - ubuntu - Torrent File RSS', items whose link is https://nyaa.si/download/<id>.torrent and pubDate 2009 for the one match

record.notes: The narrowest and most reliable feed in the sector: a saved search is a URL, and the URL returns.torrent files. Useless outside anime and East Asian media, which is why it is a second feed rather than the primary one.
